prompt:
Generate one high-quality cinematic 16:9 image for the specified section, not a generic slide or dashboard. No letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, arrows, diagrams, interface, checkmarks, traffic-light statuses or readable documents. The compositor adds every semantic mark independently. Do not invent a completed publication, a live security test, a solved outing, approval or consensus. Fictional editorial staging, not documentary evidence. Rich material detail, carefully controlled light, credible objects and hands. Keep designated annotation zones visually quiet. Never fill quiet zones with invented panels. Reference images establish cast and room identity only; follow this section's camera and blocking.
VISUAL FORMAT: doctrine-poster-and-teaser
TEACHING PURPOSE: Land the permission-versus-enforcement rule and honestly cue the next film.
CAMERA: Graphic editorial product portrait with strong negative space.
An isolated substantial brushed-metal toggle switch mounted in a small dark stone block at RIGHT CENTER, clearly separate from a blank loose paper tag lying lower left. Nothing connected, no electricity or active status, no letters or symbols. Cinematic black studio with a narrow warm rim and teal ambient depth. LEFT HALF and TOP are clean for a memorable doctrine headline. A faint abstract warm rectangular doorway far in the background can suggest a next story without depicting a booked event. Conceptual metaphor only.
COMPOSITING INTENT: Oversized rule typography dominates; the unconnected switch is the metaphor. The next-episode promise is a small distinct horizon line, not another full slide.
SEMANTIC AUTHORITY FOR CONTEXT ONLY, NEVER RENDER THESE WORDS: TAKEAWAY / REVIEW EDITION. Use the boundary evidence checklist: name the effect, bind the grant, locate the dispatcher, and test a changed condition. A permission label is not an off switch. Next, the tool succeeds. Can the agent truthfully say the task is complete?
